messages:
incidentbot: PagerDuty alert fired for service hosted-inference-api (PD-78901) at 2026-03-14T23:12:34Z. Priority: high. Primary on-call @mike did not acknowledge within 3m — alert auto-escalated to secondary @sarah. Runbook: https://redwood.dev/runbooks/hosted-inference-latency — please follow 'scale-and-route' steps.

mike: (no ack) — looks like my phone was on DND, sorry.

sarah: acked via PagerDuty. I'm taking primary investigation. pinging @timo for infra checks.

timo: seeing 95th latency jump to ~1.9s across eu-west-1. CPU on inference pods at 95%, pod restarts starting to show. Not seeing error spike, just slower responses.

sarah: ok thanks. runbook step 2 -> check autoscaler, queue length, and KV cache.

leila: flagging customer impact: two customers on premium routes reporting degraded UI load times — support ticket linked: https://support.redwood/t/4521.

sarah: noted. @ashley if this is going to be >15m might need manager escalation for customer comms.

incidentbot: PagerDuty escalation: secondary acked but no mitigation recorded after 15m — policy escalated to manager @ashley and triggered manager page.

ashley: on it, joining bridge. can someone paste the quick metrics?

timo: kubectl/top snapshot:
```
NAME                                  CPU(cores)   MEMORY(bytes)
hosted-inference-0                   1800m        11Gi
hosted-inference-1                   1700m        10.8Gi
hosted-inference-2                   1900m        11.2Gi
queue-worker-0                        400m        1.2Gi
```

and HPA shows current desired replicas=3, max=6, CPU utilization at 93%.

sarah: looks like HPA didn't scale fast enough for the sudden burst. runbook suggests scaling replicas and enabling burst pool. executing scale now.

sarah: executing: `kubectl -n prod scale deployment/hosted-inference --replicas=6`

incidentbot: action logged (user: sarah) — scaling triggered.

timo: also flipping temporary routing to dedicated-capacity for premium routes: `route update --service hosted-inference --route premium --target dedicated-pool-3`

leila: applied. support notified customers that we're investigating; ETA message queued.

sarah: tailing logs for KV cache warnings:
```
2026-03-14T23:11:50Z worker[0] WARN KVCache miss_ratio=0.87 keys=9.2e6
2026-03-14T23:12:08Z worker[1] WARN latency_token_generate=1.67s
2026-03-14T23:13:05Z scheduler ERROR backpressure: queue_wait=1400ms
```

sarah: KV cache miss rate is high -> more full-model attention work causing CPU spike. scaling + routing to dedicated pool should reduce pressure.

ashley: I'm on the bridge and I've pinged the account team for an update to impacted customers. Good call on routing. Keep timeline notes.

timo: replicas coming up; new pods reporting healthy.

incidentbot: PagerDuty note: manager @ashley acked escalated alert.

sarah: after scaling and routing, 95th latency trending down to ~420ms within 6 minutes. Monitoring charts: https://monitoring.redwood/charts/hosted-inference-api?range=30m

leila: support updated customers: "We've routed your traffic to a dedicated pool and scaled up capacity; latency improving. We'll follow-up with postmortem." (reacted :thumbsup:)

mike: sorry again for missing the initial PD page. I was on the late-night handoff and DND didn't pop. will adjust rotation notifications.

ashley: noted — we'll review paging windows and add extra PD escalation SMS for primary overnight.

sarah: final checks: no pod OOMs, memory stable, KV warming jobs are running. will keep an eye for 30m. if stable, will close PD.

incidentbot: PagerDuty: incident auto-ack close pending.

sarah: resolving in runbook: mark mitigation steps, timeline, and owner. Next: postmortem assignment to infra (owner: timo) and improve HPA tuning for bursty traffic.

timo: taking postmortem. notes: add pre-warm cache task and HPA faster ramp, consider proactive burst pool for premium traffic.

ashley: thanks all — handing back to normal ops.

sarah: resolved for now. closing thread after monitoring window. (reacted :white_check_mark:)
